title: Check yourself: Non-profits, small businesses and creative work

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A non-profit's analyst must show a funder where demand is highest, using a sheet of beneficiaries' names, addresses and health notes. Policy restricts sharing personal data. Which approach fits?

options.text: Summarise it to district counts, then verify those counts
options.says: The best answer anonymises or aggregates first and checks the results, and the funder's question needs areas, not individuals.

options.text: Paste ten full records first to test the method on a sample
options.says: Ruled out because "Donor and beneficiary records are sensitive", so ten full records are still exposure.

options.text: Switch to a faster, cheaper model for the sensitive records
options.says: Ruled out because "high-volume, low-stakes drafting suits a faster, cheaper model", and the tier chosen does not change the class of the data.

options.text: Upload the full sheet and ask Claude to leave names out of its findings
options.says: Ruled out because the rule is "classify first, remove identifiers before analysis", and leaving names out of the findings does not keep them out of the upload.

questions.stem: A small shop owner has Claude draft replies to customers about delivery times. One reply promises delivery in two days, a figure the owner never supplied. What is the best response?

options.text: Stop using Claude for customer contact altogether, starting today
options.says: Ruled out because "high-volume, low-stakes drafting suits a faster, cheaper model" with a spot check, so stopping altogether is not needed.

options.text: Send it, as the draft sounded confident and professional enough
options.says: Ruled out because the check is "that a confident reply to a customer is not invented", so confidence proves nothing.

options.text: Ask Claude whether the figure is right, and send if it agrees
options.says: Ruled out because "A small owner has no one else to catch the error", and asking the same tool whether it is right does not check the policy.

options.text: Check each date and commitment against the actual policy
options.says: A reply that states a date is a promise the owner holds, so each date is checked against the actual policy.

questions.stem: An illustrator wants to use Claude on a picture-book project and cares about being recognised for their style. Which use fits best?

options.text: Ask it to generate the whole story in their style, then sign it
options.says: Ruled out because the maker keeps "the part that makes the work theirs", and a whole story signed by the maker is not that.

options.text: Hand it production tasks, and keep the ideas and final choices
options.says: Delegate production and keep authorship, the page's guidance for makers.

options.text: Have it write the narrative and present the result as unaided work
options.says: Ruled out because "Disclosure matters more here than in many fields", and presenting AI work as unaided is the opposite.

options.text: Let it decide the visual direction, since it knows many styles
options.says: Ruled out because "For a maker the distinctive voice is the product", and the visual direction is part of it.
